steps.title: Check current litellm deployment
steps.description:
Verify your litellm version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n litellm -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm
helm list -n litellm 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working litellm installation.

steps.title: Review litellm configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant litellm configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n litellm -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm
kubectl get configmap -n litellm -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=litellm
```

steps.title: Upgrade litellm to include the fix
steps.description:
If the fix is included in a newer release, upgrade litellm:
```bash
helm repo update
helm upgrade litellm litellm/litellm --namespace litellm
```
Verify the upgrade:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n litellm
helm list -n litellm
```

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n litellm -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm
kubectl get events -n litellm --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "[Feature]: Support Python 3.14" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
Sharing what I found while looking at #27565, since that PR turned out to target the wrong cause.

The blocker for 3.14 right now is just the version cap in pyproject on litellm_internal_staging:

```toml
requires-python = ">=3.10, <3.14"
```

That's what makes 1.83.8+ reject 3.14 (1.83.7 didn't have the tightened cap). It isn't fastuuid: fastuuid 0.14.0 ships cp314 wheels and works on 3.14.
